payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #430, SLICE 2, fourth landing: decision 0068's deterministic admission pass. For each waiting entry in queue order, admission decides whether the entry may start now and records a typed reason for every one that may not. Slice 1 (the durable queue) merged as af34a5c3 (#527). #430 stays open for slices 3 to 6.

The branch story-430-slice-2 ends at 8b1ea2e1, a clean merge of main f2b3a387, which brings #423's one-test-binary layout, #500, #573 (the `--test it` gate and its runtime guard), #575 and decision 0065 slice two through U1c2. An earlier clean merge of main 8923a24c is c0673418. These are its commits, all off main 4c65f6a1:
- bc89f5e4: admission judges each waiting entry's waits (its dependencies) and its realm. It holds a drifted realm until the operator re-pins it, and `brokkr queue list` shows why.
- 30455758, 4b9eb979, 29e2939d: security-hold fix rounds. A judged drift latches until the operator re-pins it, and a re-pin takes only the map judged. A latch or re-pin is written only over the pin and latch its finding was measured against, so a peer's latch in between is refused and named. An entry queued under no map is compared too (M1).
- 428ad1e5: admission compares the realm an entry's pin selected, as recorded, never as the disk resolves its repository's path now.
- cef8ccda: an unreadable realm is refused on one path, and the latched reason is written in one write.
- 94ac5b74: the first landing's GLM review position wrote this inside its review, against its read-only charter. The operator kept it (2026-10-06), and its message says who wrote it. It cures F1 (`seen` returns the typed WorldError) and L5 (QueuedLaunch::repinned is pub(crate)).
- ce10ad73: fix round 430s2h (implement-story-430-build-decisi-de47dfd8), for H5, the first landing's hold (landing-pr-for-story-430-slice-2-c25f95ed). For an entry queued under no map, only nothing at the map path is no map. A looping link, a dangling link or a directory there holds the entry as map_unreadable, which never latches. Its review ruled residual at low.
- 1cce2cb1 (controller): the exact-coverage gate missed one branch, launch/queued.rs:176's guard on a lookup error other than NotFound. A test now pins it: a workspace that is no longer a directory holds the entry. Its removal control is in the message. On 240a485e (main edb1dbce merged), the exact-coverage gate, crap, files, clones, api, typos, shellcheck and actionlint all passed.

- ac79adb6: fix round 430s2i (implement-story-430-build-decisi-81da5a99), for H6, the second landing's hold (landing-pr-for-story-430-slice-2-6ebca740). Admission selects the realm on disk ONCE. Now carries the map on disk as a Held (the world and the realm selected in it, resolved through one closure seam, held_and_now_with), the digest is the pin_of that one selection, and `seen` reads both sides through Held::selection, never calling realm_for again. A repository retargeted mid-judgement is judged on one selection, and the re-pin under the map as it then stands is refused MapMoved. The same commit makes Released's field and brokkr-store's Latch::seq, Seen::latch, Seen::pin and QueueEntry::pin pub(crate) (L5-API). Its review ruled residual at low.
- 022f70e7 and 6ec7c415 (controller): the exact-coverage gate on ac79adb6 missed one line, MapSource::digest's Unmapped arm, now reached only through a re-pin. A test pins it: an unmapped entry held and latched when a map came, whose map is gone again by the re-pin, is refused MapMoved. Its removal control (`shown` letting a None digest through) failed the test. The second commit folds the two MapMoved assertions into one helper, for the clone ratchet.

- 2e532547 (controller): the third landing (landing-pr-for-story-430-slice-2-b93999a0) ruled residual at LOW with no security residual, and its exact-coverage gate passed. But the host lint `typos --hidden` refused the new row's name ("entrys"). The row is renamed an_unmapped_entry_is_not_repinned_once_the_map_that_held_it_is_gone, with its body unchanged. This rename and the merge of main are the only changes since the third landing's vouch.

What slice 2 does NOT judge yet, and the PR says so: provider and route concurrency and cooldowns, the scratch-space floor and the boxed-build ceiling. admission.rs:38-41 defers them, because decision 0068 declares them in the realm's host configuration, which the realms map does not carry yet. The first landing's commission wrongly said bc89f5e4 judged them; correct the record wherever you quote it.

The operator's rulings this slice builds, each recorded on #430:
- Realm drift, option C (2026-10-04). Admission compares the pinned map's governing facts (grants as whole values, boundary, house rules, dialect) with the map on disk. On a difference it HOLDS the entry with a typed reason naming each difference. Only the operator resolves a held entry ("whatever actor holds the operator's authority"), by a journaled command: release under the map now (re-pin), re-queue or drop. Admission never resolves a difference itself.
- M1 (2026-10-04). An entry queued with no realms map is compared like any other, and a map that now names its repository holds it.

The PR's Ruling line will ask the operator for the public API growth of slice 2's surface: quality/public-api/brokkr-runtime.txt +74 lines (1542 → 1616, the admission module) and brokkr-store.txt +16 lines (173 → 189, queue latches and re-pins, after L5-API narrowed four fields). Check each line is this slice's and no larger than it needs. admission.rs is a new file at 798 lines, under the 800 ceiling, so it needs no file-size raise.

Judge:
1. That admission never starts on a stale grant and never silently takes a loosened one. Grants compare as whole values, so a key added later (0065 slice two's `retain` under realms v8, when it lands) holds an entry with no change here. Tightened and loosened drift, the re-pin, a peer's interleaved latch, an unreadable map and an entry queued unmapped each hold or refuse as the rulings say, each bound by a test whose mutation fails it.
2. That admission observes the realm on disk once per entry and decides on that one observation (H6): the digest a latch records and the differences it records come from one selection, under any retarget between reads. And that the unmapped edge tells absence from a map path that cannot be read: nothing there is admissible, and anything else (a link that loops or dangles, a directory, a lookup that errs) holds unlatched. Say whether any other path reads an unreadable map as no map.
3. That admission is deterministic: the same journal, map and host facts give the same decision and the same reasons, in queue order.
4. That the merge with main changes neither side's behaviour. `brokkr queue` (slice 1's verbs), `brokkr run` and 0065 slice two's compile and launch paths behave as on main. Since #423 each crate's integration tests are one binary (`--test it FILE::`). This slice adds no tests/*.rs file, and the layering::test_targets gate passes.
5. That the carried LOWs are listed for the PR: L1 (Governing holds house and dialect as serde_json::Value), L4 (judge commits each latch in its own transaction; slice 3's fence), and the inherited slice-1 debt.
6. That nothing here spawns a queued run unattended. That is slice 3. Say whether any explicit start path exists and, if so, that it goes through slice 1's rebuild and launch::start, as `brokkr run` does.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy on the crates you touched, with -D warnings
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files, clones, crap and api

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

members.adversarial:
Read-only adversarial review at 8b1ea2e1 against merged main f2b3a387, including all slice-2 changes and the fourth-landing delta. No new concrete behavioral or security finding. The only slice change since the third landing is the test-name correction; the merge has no remerge conflict diff. No tracked file changed, no source mutation planted, no fix or commit made.

Carried LOWs for the PR: L1 (decision 0071 ruling 3), admission.rs Governing.house/dialect remain serde_json::Value read by string key in unplaced. The implementer's reason remains whole-fact comparison excluding source paths, with shared pin typing deferred to the realms work. L4 (ruling 10): two drifted entries A then B are measured; if a peer replaces B's pin/latch before its write, A's latch can commit before B refuses Unmeasured, so judge returns an error without verdicts despite A's durable write. Each individual latch remains fenced and sound; slice 3 owes the larger fence. Inherited slice-1 LOW debt remains: HeldWorld(Value) and its always-a-world fallback lack the named removal-control test (rulings 3/9); rebuild and queue_claim still have only test consumers, with slice 3 named as their production caller (ruling 6); hold/release validate only their target, UnknownWord is nested in a SQLite conversion error, and nonnumeric queue_schema is reported as 0 (rulings 3/8). The old unsupported-version repair defect is cured, not carried.

Judgments: whole CapabilityGrant equality holds tightened, loosened and extra-key drift. Recorded held selection is never resolved again. Now::of selects the current realm once into Held; both candidate digest and differences use that selection, with seen making no second realm_for call (rulings 2/10). The H6 test retargets the repository during selection and asserts the exact consistent Finding and MapMoved refusal. A-B-A drift stays latched across reopen; re-pin requires the judged digest and fences both pin and latch inside its write transaction. Peer latch/pin replacements are refused and named. Stable journal/map/filesystem facts yield deterministic queue order and reason order through explicit SQL ordering, exhaustive status matching and BTree collections. The relevant compiling removal controls and failing tests are recorded in commit history; inspected, not replanted under this read-only charter (ruling 9).

Unreadable maps: unmapped admission treats only symlink_metadata NotFound as absence. Looping/dangling links, directories and other lookup errors hold unlatched; mapped reads and re-pin do not fall back to no map. Outside admission, unchanged World::discover/inspect use is_file and can treat those ambient paths as absent, including direct run and initial queue add. Subsequent queued admission uses the stricter edge. No new admission path bypasses it.

Merge/scope: direct-run, compile/protocol paths and test-target implementation match merged main; World::pin delegation and TextPin serialization preserve their output. Existing queue verbs retain their state behavior with the intended admission readout. Frozen contracts, fixtures, reference and policy/phase-machine.json have no diff; this slice adds no tests/*.rs file. API growth is exactly runtime +74 (1542 to 1616), entirely admission, and store +16 (173 to 189), consumed queue read/latch/re-pin types, methods and refusals. Narrowed fields remain crate-private; no further unnecessary public growth found. admission.rs is 798 lines (rulings 4/6).

Nothing starts queued runs unattended, and no queue start verb exists.
